question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

A lot of social work is hindered due to corrupt politicians.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Obstructed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hindered" means created difficulties for someone or something, resulting in delay or obstruction; blocked the progress of. Its closest synonym is "obstructed". (बाधित किया / रोका)

◦ Correct: A lot of social work is hindered/obstructed due to corrupt politicians.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Collided" (crashed into) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "Helped" (assisted) is an antonym.

• Option 4 "Abided" (obeyed/endured) does not fit.

NOTE

• Synonyms of hinder: obstruct, impede, hamper, block, thwart, delay. Antonyms: help, aid, assist, facilitate, promote.

question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.

The dog is the most faithful animal.
option_1: The dog is more useful than any other animal.
option_2: The dog is the faithful animal.
option_3: No other animal is as faithful as the dog.
option_4: The dog is the only faithful animal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No other animal is as faithful as the dog.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The superlative "the most faithful animal" is changed into the positive degree using the structure "No other + noun + is as + positive adjective + as + subject".

◦ Superlative: The dog is the most faithful animal.

◦ Positive: No other animal is as faithful as the dog.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 changes the adjective to "useful" and gives a comparative form, altering the meaning.

• Options 2 and 4 do not preserve the superlative sense in the positive degree.

NOTE

• Degree change of "The dog is the most faithful animal":

◦ Superlative: The dog is the most faithful animal.

◦ Comparative: The dog is more faithful than any other animal.

◦ Positive: No other animal is as faithful as the dog.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

My mother is 51 years old, / and my uncle is 48 years old. / So my mother is old than my uncle.
option_2: and my uncle is 48 years old.
option_3: So my mother is old than my uncle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. So my mother is old than my uncle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" is a marker of the comparative degree, so the adjective "old" must become its comparative form "older". So the segment should be "So my mother is older than my uncle".

◦ Correct: So my mother is older than my uncle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "My mother is 51 years old," and "and my uncle is 48 years old." are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Degrees of "old": old (positive) – older/elder (comparative, with "than") – oldest/eldest (superlative). Use "older/oldest" for things and people; "elder/eldest" only for people within a family, without "than".

question:
Based on the context of the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Siri was feeling ____________ after receiving praise from her professor for completing the project ahead of schedule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. on top of the world.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "on top of the world" means extremely happy, delighted and proud. Receiving praise for finishing early would make Siri feel very happy. (अत्यंत प्रसन्न / गर्वित)

◦ Correct: Siri was feeling on top of the world after receiving praise from her professor ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "under the weather" (feeling unwell), Option 2 "in the dark" (unaware/uninformed) and Option 3 "in the same boat" (in the same difficult situation) do not fit a moment of praise.

NOTE

• Idioms of great happiness: "on cloud nine", "over the moon", "walking on air", "in seventh heaven", "on top of the world".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My sister is allergic with peanuts, so be cautious when preparing her meal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. allergic with peanuts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "allergic" takes the preposition "to", not "with". So the correct phrase is "allergic to peanuts".

◦ Correct: My sister is allergic to peanuts, so be cautious when preparing her meal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "My sister is", "so be cautious" and "when preparing her meal." are all correct.

NOTE

• Fixed adjective + preposition combinations: allergic to, afraid of, good at, fond of, angry with (a person)/about (a thing), interested in.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

The mountain peak offers a breathtaking view, a striking contrast to the ___________(peculiar) scenery below.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ordinary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Peculiar" means strange, unusual or odd. Its antonym is "ordinary" (normal, common, usual). The sentence needs a contrast to the "breathtaking view", so "ordinary scenery below" fits. (विचित्र का विलोम — साधारण)

◦ Correct: ... a striking contrast to the ordinary scenery below.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 3 "abnormal" and 4 "odd" are synonyms of peculiar, not antonyms.

• Option 1 "beautiful" is not the direct antonym of "peculiar".

NOTE

• Synonyms of peculiar: strange, odd, unusual, abnormal, bizarre. Antonyms: ordinary, normal, common, usual, familiar.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Regal
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Majestic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Regal" means relating to or resembling a king or queen; splendid and dignified. Its closest synonym is "majestic". (शाही / राजसी)

◦ Example: The queen made a regal/majestic entrance into the hall.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "Ordinary", 3 "Modest" and 4 "Humble" all suggest plainness or lack of grandeur, which are antonyms of regal.

NOTE

• Synonyms of regal: majestic, royal, kingly, stately, grand, imposing. Antonyms: humble, modest, ordinary, lowly.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The poet had to draw on his fancy to write all his sonnets.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. use his imagination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "draw on (one's) fancy" means to use one's imagination / creative power. Here "fancy" is used in the sense of imagination. (कल्पनाशक्ति का उपयोग करना)

◦ Correct: The poet had to draw on his fancy (use his imagination) to write all his sonnets.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Draw on" means to make use of a resource; "fancy" (as a noun) can mean imagination. So the phrase means to use one's imagination.

• Options 1, 2 and 4 do not match the meaning of "fancy".

NOTE

• A "sonnet" is a 14-line poem. Related expressions: "a flight of fancy" (an unrealistic idea), "take a fancy to" (to start liking).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'opacity' in the given sentence.

The diminishing and deteriorating visibility in winter leads to the revival of accident cases on the highway.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. visibility.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Opacity" means the quality of being opaque; the condition of not allowing light to pass through; lack of clarity/transparency. Its antonym is "visibility" (the state of being able to see or be seen clearly). (अपारदर्शिता का विलोम — दृश्यता)

◦ Opacity blocks sight, whereas visibility allows clear sight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "diminishing", 3 "revival" and 4 "deteriorating" are not opposites of "opacity".

NOTE

• Synonyms of opacity: obscurity, cloudiness, murkiness, opaqueness. Antonyms: transparency, clarity, visibility, translucence.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

She tried not to embarras her friend by bringing up the awkward incident at the party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. embarrass.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word "embarras" should be spelt "embarrass", meaning to make someone feel awkward, ashamed or self-conscious. (शर्मिंदा करना)

• Spelling key: EM + BAR + RASS — it has double "r" and double "s".

◦ Correct: She tried not to embarrass her friend ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "embarress", 2 "emberrass" and 3 "embarass" are all wrong spellings.

NOTE

• Remember the "double-double" rule: embarrass (rr, ss), embarrassment, embarrassing. Related tricky words: "harass" has one "r" and one "s".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Shyam approached an leading psychologist for his treatment of anxiety and depression.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. an leading psychologist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article "an" is used before a word beginning with a vowel sound. "leading" begins with the consonant sound /l/, so the article "a" must be used — "a leading psychologist".

◦ Correct: Shyam approached a leading psychologist for his treatment of anxiety and depression.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Shyam approached", "for his treatment" and "of anxiety and depression." are all correct.

NOTE

• Article rule (sound, not spelling): use "a" before a consonant sound (a leading, a university, a one-rupee coin) and "an" before a vowel sound (an hour, an MRI, an honest man).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Our team lost the game / only because of / a mistake / with one of our players.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. with one of our players.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A mistake is made "by" a person, not "with" a person. The correct preposition is "by" — "a mistake by one of our players".

◦ Correct: Our team lost the game only because of a mistake by one of our players.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Our team lost the game", "only because of" and "a mistake" are all correct.

NOTE

• "By" indicates the doer/agent of an action (a mistake by him, a novel written by her), whereas "with" indicates an instrument or accompaniment (cut with a knife, went with a friend).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Ramgopal is having a very big house in Mumbai.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. has.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Have/has" in the sense of possession is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous (–ing) form. So "is having" (possession) is wrong; the correct form is the simple present "has".

◦ Correct: Ramgopal has a very big house in Mumbai.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "have" does not agree with the singular subject "Ramgopal" (needs "has").

• Option 4 "were having" is a wrong past continuous form.

NOTE

• Stative verbs (of possession, emotion, senses) are not normally used in continuous tense: have (own), know, believe, like, love, want. "Having" is allowed only when it means an activity — "having lunch", "having a bath".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Her presentation was both informative and __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. entertaining.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correlative "both ... and" joins parallel elements. Since "informative" is an adjective, the second word must also be an adjective — "entertaining".

◦ Correct: Her presentation was both informative and entertaining.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "entertainer" is a noun; Option 2 "entertain" is a verb; Option 3 "entertainingly" is an adverb — none is parallel to the adjective "informative".

NOTE

• "Both ... and" must join grammatically equal parts (adjective + adjective, noun + noun, verb + verb). Here: informative (adj.) + entertaining (adj.).

question:
Select the most appropriate article to fill in the blank. Select 'no article' if no article is required.

The doctor asked the patient to have _____ MRI scan of his brain.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. an.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article is chosen by sound, not spelling. "MRI" begins with the letter "M", but is pronounced "em-ar-eye", starting with the vowel sound /e/. Hence "an" is used — "an MRI scan".

◦ Correct: The doctor asked the patient to have an MRI scan of his brain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "a" is wrong because MRI starts with a vowel sound.

• "the" and "no article" do not suit the first-mention, singular countable noun "MRI scan".

NOTE

• "an" before vowel-sound abbreviations: an MRI, an MP, an MLA, an SP, an X-ray, an FIR. "a" before consonant-sound ones: a UNESCO team, a university.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

They had a least celebration on her birthday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. little.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Celebration" (used here as an uncountable idea of festivity) needs the quantifier "little" (meaning "a small amount of"), not the superlative "least". So the correct phrase is "a little celebration".

◦ Correct: They had a little celebration on her birthday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "less" and Option 4 "lesser" are comparatives that do not fit with the article "a".

• Option 2 "most less" is a grammatically incorrect double form.

NOTE

• "A little" = a small quantity (positive sense) of an uncountable noun: a little water, a little celebration. "Little" (without "a") means hardly any (negative sense).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

A person who does not believe in the institution of marriage
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Misogamist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Misogamist" is a person who hates or does not believe in the institution of marriage. (विवाह से घृणा करने वाला)

◦ Root: "misos" (hatred) + "gamos" (marriage).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Nihilist" — one who believes life is meaningless / rejects all moral principles.

• Option 3 "Masochist" — one who enjoys their own pain or suffering.

• Option 4 "Misogynist" — one who hates women.

NOTE

• Related "miso-" words: misogamist (hates marriage), misogynist (hates women), misandrist (hates men), misanthrope (hates mankind/humanity).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word.

The board will look into the matter.
option_3: A group of members of a company
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A group of members of a company.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "board" means the "Board of Directors" — a group of people (members) who manage or govern a company or organisation. (निदेशक मंडल)

◦ Correct: The board (group of members of a company) will look into the matter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "A union of workers" describes a trade union.

• Option 2 "A member of a family" and Option 4 "A group of elected politicians" (e.g., a legislature) do not match "board".

NOTE

• "Look into" is a phrasal verb meaning to investigate/examine. A "board" can also mean a flat plank, a committee, or meals ("board and lodging"), depending on context.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Exagerate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Exagerate" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "exaggerate" (with double "g"), meaning to represent something as larger, better or worse than it really is; to overstate. (अतिशयोक्ति करना)

• Spelling key: EX + AGG + ER + ATE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Unnecessary" (double n), "Argument" (no "e" after "u") and "Misinterpret" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related: exaggerate (verb), exaggeration (noun), exaggerated (adjective) — all keep the double "g". A common error is writing a single "g".

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

A) Occasion   B) Privilege   C) Bizzare   D) Definitely
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. C (the word "Bizzare").

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the listed words, the incorrectly spelt one is item C — "Bizzare". The correct spelling is "bizarre" (with one "z" and double "r"), meaning very strange or unusual. (विचित्र)

• Since the misspelt word is item C, the answer option that gives "C" is Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other words are correctly spelt: Occasion (double "c", single "s"), Privilege (no "d", ends "-ilege") and Definitely ("finite" inside it — de-finite-ly).

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt words: bizarre (not "bizzare"), privilege (not "priviledge"), definitely (not "definately"), occasion (not "occassion").

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Speaking is a powerful tool (1)________ human communication. It allows us to convey thoughts, emotions and ideas to others. Effective speaking (2)_________ not only the words we choose but also our tone, body language and overall presentation. Public speaking, in particular, can be (3)______ a skill and an art, enabling individuals to inspire, educate and persuade audiences. (4)________ it is a casual conversation with a friend or a formal presentation to a large group, the ability to express (5)_________ clearly and confidently through speaking is a valuable skill that can greatly impact our personal and professional lives.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. for.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "for" correctly shows purpose/use — speaking is a powerful tool "for human communication" (i.e., used for the purpose of communicating). (के लिए)

◦ Correct: Speaking is a powerful tool for human communication.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "a tool for (a purpose)" is the natural collocation. "at", "on" and "with" do not convey purpose here and sound unidiomatic.

NOTE

• "A tool for + purpose/gerund": a tool for learning, a tool for communication, a platform for discussion. "For" often expresses purpose or intended use.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Speaking is a powerful tool (1)________ human communication. It allows us to convey thoughts, emotions and ideas to others. Effective speaking (2)_________ not only the words we choose but also our tone, body language and overall presentation. Public speaking, in particular, can be (3)______ a skill and an art, enabling individuals to inspire, educate and persuade audiences. (4)________ it is a casual conversation with a friend or a formal presentation to a large group, the ability to express (5)_________ clearly and confidently through speaking is a valuable skill that can greatly impact our personal and professional lives.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. involves.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Effective speaking" is singular, so the verb in the simple present must take "-s" — "involves" (subject-verb agreement).

◦ Correct: Effective speaking involves not only the words we choose but also our tone ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "involve" (plural verb) does not agree with the singular subject.

• Options 3 "involving" and 4 "involved" cannot stand as the main finite verb here.

NOTE

• Subject-verb agreement: a singular subject takes a singular verb (speaking involves). Uncountable/gerund subjects like "speaking" are treated as singular.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Speaking is a powerful tool (1)________ human communication. It allows us to convey thoughts, emotions and ideas to others. Effective speaking (2)_________ not only the words we choose but also our tone, body language and overall presentation. Public speaking, in particular, can be (3)______ a skill and an art, enabling individuals to inspire, educate and persuade audiences. (4)________ it is a casual conversation with a friend or a formal presentation to a large group, the ability to express (5)_________ clearly and confidently through speaking is a valuable skill that can greatly impact our personal and professional lives.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. both.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correlative conjunction "both ... and" is needed here, joining "a skill" and "an art". The blank supplies the first half "both" (which pairs with the "and" that follows).

◦ Correct: Public speaking, in particular, can be both a skill and an art ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "and" alone does not fit before "a skill ... and an art" (it would leave the structure incomplete).

• Options 3 "until" and 4 "though" do not suit the meaning.

NOTE

• "Both ... and" emphasises two things together. The words it joins must be parallel: both a skill and an art (noun + noun).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Speaking is a powerful tool (1)________ human communication. It allows us to convey thoughts, emotions and ideas to others. Effective speaking (2)_________ not only the words we choose but also our tone, body language and overall presentation. Public speaking, in particular, can be (3)______ a skill and an art, enabling individuals to inspire, educate and persuade audiences. (4)________ it is a casual conversation with a friend or a formal presentation to a large group, the ability to express (5)_________ clearly and confidently through speaking is a valuable skill that can greatly impact our personal and professional lives.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Whether.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Whether ... or" expresses two alternatives. The sentence contrasts "a casual conversation with a friend" or "a formal presentation to a large group", so "Whether" is correct.

◦ Correct: Whether it is a casual conversation with a friend or a formal presentation to a large group ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Neither" pairs with "nor" (not "or"); Option 2 "Whereas" and Option 3 "Because" do not fit the "... or ..." structure that follows.

NOTE

• "Whether ... or" introduces two possibilities, both leading to the same result. Do not confuse "whether" (alternatives) with "weather" (climate).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Speaking is a powerful tool (1)________ human communication. It allows us to convey thoughts, emotions and ideas to others. Effective speaking (2)_________ not only the words we choose but also our tone, body language and overall presentation. Public speaking, in particular, can be (3)______ a skill and an art, enabling individuals to inspire, educate and persuade audiences. (4)________ it is a casual conversation with a friend or a formal presentation to a large group, the ability to express (5)_________ clearly and confidently through speaking is a valuable skill that can greatly impact our personal and professional lives.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ourselves.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Earlier the passage uses "we" and "our" (the words we choose, our tone), so the reflexive pronoun must agree with the first-person plural — "ourselves". "express ourselves" means to convey one's own thoughts/feelings.

◦ Correct: ... the ability to express ourselves clearly and confidently through speaking ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "itself", Option 3 "themselves" and Option 4 "herself" do not agree with the first-person plural reference established by "we/our".

NOTE

• Reflexive pronouns must match their antecedent in person and number: I–myself, we–ourselves, you–yourself/yourselves, he–himself, she–herself, it–itself, they–themselves. "Express oneself" = to put one's thoughts into words.

question: In December 2023, who became the first women Chief of Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nina Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In December 2023, IPS officer Nina Singh became the first woman Director General (Chief) of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF). (नीना सिंह — CISF की पहली महिला महानिदेशक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The CISF is a Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) under the Ministry of Home Affairs, raised in 1969. It guards airports, metros, nuclear and space installations, ports and other vital establishments.

• Nina Singh is a 1989-batch IPS officer of the Rajasthan cadre.

NOTE

• Archana Ramasundaram was the first woman DG of a paramilitary force (SSB) in 2016. The CISF's motto is "Protection and Security".

question: The autobiography, 'An Autobiography' by Jawaharlal Nehru is also known as ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Toward Freedom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jawaharlal Nehru's work "An Autobiography" (1936) is also known as "Toward Freedom". He wrote it largely during his imprisonment in 1934–35. (नेहरू की आत्मकथा — Toward Freedom)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other famous works by Nehru: "The Discovery of India", "Glimpses of World History" and "Letters from a Father to His Daughter".

• Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister (1947–1964); his birthday, 14 November, is celebrated as Children's Day.

NOTE

• "The Accidental Prime Minister" was written by Sanjaya Baru (on Manmohan Singh). "The Unfinished Innings" is not associated with Nehru.

question: In which of the following states is the groundnut fair, 'Kadalekayi Parishe' celebrated on the last Monday of the Karthika month of the Hindu calendar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kadalekayi Parishe" (the groundnut fair) is a traditional fair celebrated in Bengaluru, Karnataka, on the last Monday of the Karthika month. Farmers offer the first crop of groundnuts to Lord Basavanna (the Nandi bull). (कदलेकायी परिशे — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The fair is held around the Bull Temple (Dodda Basavana Gudi) in Basavanagudi, Bengaluru.

• "Kadalekayi" means groundnut/peanut in Kannada; "Parishe" means fair.

NOTE

• Other fairs of India: Pushkar Fair (Rajasthan), Sonepur Cattle Fair (Bihar), Hemis Festival (Ladakh).

question: The earthquakes that are generated due to the explosion of chemical or nuclear devices are known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Explosion earthquakes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Explosion earthquakes" are the earthquakes caused by the detonation of chemical or nuclear devices. The ground shakes due to the energy released by the explosion. (विस्फोट भूकंप)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Tectonic earthquakes — caused by the movement of tectonic plates (the most common type).

• Volcanic earthquakes — associated with volcanic activity.

• Collapse earthquakes — caused by the collapse of underground caverns/mines.

• Reservoir-induced earthquakes — caused by the pressure of water in large dams/reservoirs.

NOTE

• Earthquakes are measured by the Richter scale (magnitude) and their intensity by the Mercalli scale. The instrument used is the seismograph.

question: Which of the following gases is generally used to flush bags of chips by the manufacturers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitrogen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nitrogen" gas is used to flush (fill) bags of chips. Being an inert (non-reactive) gas, it prevents the chips from being oxidised (going rancid), keeps them crisp, and cushions them against breakage. (नाइट्रोजन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Nitrogen (N₂) makes up about 78% of the Earth's atmosphere and is chemically inert at normal temperatures.

• Oxygen would spoil the food by oxidation, so it is deliberately removed.

NOTE

• Uses of nitrogen: food packaging, making ammonia (Haber process), liquid nitrogen for freezing, and filling tyres. Its symbol is N, atomic number 7.

question: In the year 1940, the national games were hosted by which of the following cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the year 1940, the National Games of India were hosted by the city of Bombay (now Mumbai). (1940 के राष्ट्रीय खेल — बंबई/मुंबई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The National Games of India are a multi-sport event featuring athletes from different states and union territories.

• The Games were first held (as the Indian Olympic Games) in 1924 at Lahore.

NOTE

• Recent editions: the 36th National Games were held in Gujarat (2022) and the 37th in Goa (2023).

question: Who among the following was the founder of 'Satnami movement' in the central India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghasidas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Ghasidas founded the "Satnami movement" in central India (the Chhattisgarh region) in the early 19th century. He preached the worship of one formless God ("Satnam" — the true name) and opposed caste discrimination and untouchability. (गुरु घासीदास — सतनामी आंदोलन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Guru Ghasidas worked among the Chamar community, promoting equality, truth and rejection of idol worship and rituals.

• The Guru Ghasidas National Park in Chhattisgarh is named after him.

NOTE

• There was also an earlier Satnami sect founded by Birbhan in the 17th century (Narnaul region), which revolted against Aurangzeb in 1672.

question: What does a budget deficit indicate?
option_1: The government is saving for future projects
option_2: The government is not allocating enough funds for public services
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government spending exceeds government revenue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "budget deficit" occurs when the government's total expenditure (spending) exceeds its total revenue (income) in a given period. (बजट घाटा — व्यय > राजस्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• When revenue exceeds spending, it is a budget surplus; when they are equal, it is a balanced budget.

• Governments often finance a deficit through borrowing (loans, bonds).

NOTE

• Related terms: Fiscal Deficit (total expenditure – total revenue excluding borrowings), Revenue Deficit, and Primary Deficit (fiscal deficit – interest payments).

question: In which of the following years was the state of Golconda finally annexed into the Mughal empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1687.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Golconda Sultanate (ruled by the Qutb Shahi dynasty) was finally annexed into the Mughal Empire in 1687 by Emperor Aurangzeb. (गोलकुंडा का मुगल साम्राज्य में विलय — 1687)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Aurangzeb had annexed the Bijapur Sultanate (Adil Shahi dynasty) in 1686, just a year earlier.

• Golconda (near Hyderabad) was famous for its diamonds (including the Kohinoor) and its strong fort.

NOTE

• The Deccan Sultanates were: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar and Berar, formed after the break-up of the Bahmani Kingdom.

question: Palkigundu Minor Rock Edicts of Ashoka are located in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Palkigundu (Pakligundu) Minor Rock Edicts" of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka are located in the Koppal district of Karnataka. (अशोक के पलकीगुंडु लघु शिलालेख — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Many of Ashoka's Minor Rock Edicts are found in Karnataka (e.g., at Maski, Brahmagiri, Gavimath, Palkigundu, Siddapura, Jatinga-Rameshwara).

• The Maski and Gujarra edicts are important because they mention Ashoka by his personal name "Ashoka (Devanampiya Asoka)".

NOTE

• Ashoka's edicts were mostly written in the Brahmi script and Prakrit language. They were first deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

question: The Great Granary was one of the largest granaries in the _______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harappan Civilization.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Great Granary" was one of the largest structures of the Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilization, found at Mohenjo-daro (and a similar granary at Harappa). It was used to store surplus grain. (हड़प्पा सभ्यता — विशाल अन्नागार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Great Bath (a large public water tank) was also found at Mohenjo-daro.

• The Harappan Civilization (c. 2500 BCE) flourished along the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra rivers and is known for town planning, drainage and standardised bricks.

NOTE

• Important Harappan sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal (dockyard), Kalibangan (ploughed field), Rakhigarhi.

question: Who among the following Indian dancers was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 1971, who was also known as the father of modern Indian dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Uday Shankar, honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 1971, is regarded as the "father of modern Indian dance". He created a unique style blending classical Indian dance with European techniques. (उदय शंकर — आधुनिक भारतीय नृत्य के जनक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Uday Shankar was the elder brother of the sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar.

• His famous film "Kalpana (1948)" showcased his innovative dance style.

NOTE

• Pandit Birju Maharaj was a legend of Kathak; Kelucharan Mohapatra was a maestro of Odissi; Pandit Durga Lal was a noted Kathak dancer.

question: As on February 2024, Nitish Kumar is the 9th time Chief Minister of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As on February 2024, Nitish Kumar took oath as the Chief Minister of Bihar for the 9th time. (नीतीश कुमार — बिहार के मुख्यमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nitish Kumar is the leader of the Janata Dal (United) [JD(U)] party.

• Bihar's capital is Patna; its Governor (as of that period) and the CM head the state executive.

NOTE

• The Chief Minister is the real executive head of a state, appointed by the Governor under Article 164 of the Constitution.

question: In the 1974 edition of the Guinness Book of Records, which playback singer was mentioned as the most recorded artist in human history?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lata Mangeshkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the 1974 edition of the Guinness Book of Records, the legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar was mentioned as the most recorded artist in human history. (लता मंगेशकर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lata Mangeshkar (the "Nightingale of India") received the Bharat Ratna (2001), the Dadasaheb Phalke Award and numerous other honours.

• She sang in many Indian languages over a career spanning several decades.

NOTE

• P. Susheela and K. S. Chithra are celebrated South Indian playback singers, also recognised by Guinness for a large number of recorded songs.

question: What is the female literacy rate in India, as per the 2011 census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 65.46%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of 2011, the female literacy rate in India was 65.46%. (2011 जनगणना — महिला साक्षरता दर 65.46%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The overall literacy rate in 2011 was 74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female at 65.46%.

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate; Bihar the lowest.

NOTE

• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census; its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future". Literacy is defined as the ability to read and write with understanding in any language, for those aged 7 and above.

question: Forward Bloc was founded in 1939-40 by which of the following leaders?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhash Chandra Bose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "All India Forward Bloc" was founded by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1939 (formally in 1940), after he resigned as the President of the Indian National Congress. (फॉरवर्ड ब्लॉक — सुभाष चंद्र बोस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Subhas Chandra Bose had won the Congress Presidency at Tripuri (1939) defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya, but resigned due to differences with Gandhiji.

• He later organised the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) and gave the slogan "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom".

NOTE

• Rash Behari Bose helped establish the INA/Indian Independence League in East Asia. Bose is fondly called "Netaji"; 23 January (his birthday) is observed as Parakram Diwas.

question: Dandiya Raas is a famous dance form of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dandiya Raas" is a famous folk dance of the state of Gujarat, performed with decorated sticks (dandiyas), especially during the festival of Navratri. (डांडिया रास — गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Garba" is another popular folk dance of Gujarat associated with Navratri; in 2023, Garba was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

• Dandiya Raas symbolises a playful, mock-fight dance associated with Goddess Durga and Lord Krishna.

NOTE

• Folk dances: Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Bihu (Assam), Garba/Dandiya (Gujarat), Lavani (Maharashtra).

question: Which of the following is/are the highest judiciary in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Supreme Court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Supreme Court of India" is the highest judicial body (apex court) in India. It is the final court of appeal and the guardian of the Constitution. (सर्वोच्च न्यायालय — भारत की सर्वोच्च न्यायपालिका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Supreme Court was established on 28 January 1950 and is located in New Delhi.

• The judicial hierarchy is: Supreme Court → High Courts → District/Subordinate Courts.

NOTE

• Articles 124–147 deal with the Supreme Court. The Chief Justice of India (CJI) heads it. Judges are appointed by the President and retire at the age of 65.

question: The Mayurbhanj District in Odisha is a part of which Biosphere Reserve from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Similipal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mayurbhanj district of Odisha is home to the "Similipal Biosphere Reserve", which includes the Similipal Tiger Reserve and National Park. (सिमिलिपाल बायोस्फीयर रिज़र्व — मयूरभंज, ओडिशा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Similipal is famous for its melanistic (black) tigers, elephants, waterfalls (Barehipani, Joranda) and rich sal forests.

• It was designated a Biosphere Reserve in 1994 and is part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves (2009).

NOTE

• Other biosphere reserves: Dehang-Debang (Arunachal Pradesh), Pachmarhi (Madhya Pradesh), Nokrek (Meghalaya), Nilgiri (India's first, 1986).

question: As per Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, what is the total length of National Highways in India as of November 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1,44,634 kilometres.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), the total length of National Highways in India as of November 2022 was about 1,44,634 kilometres. (राष्ट्रीय राजमार्गों की लंबाई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• National Highways form only a small share of the total road network but carry a large share of the traffic.

• India has one of the largest road networks in the world; road transport is managed by MoRTH and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

NOTE

• The NHAI was set up in 1988. NH 44 (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) is the longest National Highway in India.

question: Which of the following neighbouring countries of India is most populous?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given neighbouring countries of India, "Pakistan" is the most populous (with a population of over 24 crore/240 million), higher than Bangladesh, Afghanistan and Bhutan. (पाकिस्तान — सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India shares land borders with Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Afghanistan.

• Bangladesh (~17 crore) is the next most populous among the options, followed by Afghanistan and then Bhutan (least populous).

NOTE

• India's longest land border is with Bangladesh (~4,096 km); the border with Pakistan is guarded by the Border Security Force (BSF).

question: Who among the following athletes was conferred with the Arjuna Award, 2021 by President Ram Nath Kovind?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arpinder Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arpinder Singh, the Indian triple jump athlete, was conferred with the Arjuna Award in 2021 by President Ram Nath Kovind. (अर्पिंदर सिंह — अर्जुन पुरस्कार 2021)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Arpinder Singh won the gold medal in triple jump at the 2018 Asian Games (Jakarta).

• The Arjuna Award is given for outstanding performance in sports over a period of years (usually four years).

NOTE

• India's top sports honours: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (highest), Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award (coaches), Dhyan Chand Award (lifetime achievement).

question: Which of the following is the federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bicameralism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bicameralism" (a two-house Parliament — the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, the latter representing the states) is a federal feature of the Indian Constitution. (द्विसदनीयता — संघीय विशेषता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Federal features: written Constitution, division of powers (Union, State and Concurrent lists), supremacy of the Constitution, independent judiciary and bicameralism.

• Unitary features: single citizenship, integrated judiciary, All-India Services, strong Centre and emergency provisions.

NOTE

• The Indian Constitution is described as "federal in form but unitary in spirit" (a quasi-federal Constitution). The term "Federation" is not used; Article 1 calls India a "Union of States".

question: When a sailor jumps out of a rowing boat, the boat moves backwards. This represents:
solution_text:
The correct answer is the First law of motion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Per the given official key, when a sailor jumps out of a rowing boat and the boat moves backwards, it is treated as an illustration of the First law of motion (law of inertia) — the action of the sailor changes the state of the boat's rest. (न्यूटन का पहला गति नियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia): a body continues in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.

• Newton's Second Law: Force = mass × acceleration (F = ma).

• Newton's Third Law: to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

NOTE

• The recoil of a boat/gun and the motion of a rocket are classic examples used to illustrate Newton's laws of motion; conceptually the boat's backward motion also relates to conservation of momentum.

question: When the body is deprived of energy from food, which of the following tissues is used to feed on its own?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adipose tissue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adipose tissue" (a type of connective tissue that stores fat) is used by the body as a reserve energy source when it is deprived of energy from food. Stored fat is broken down to release energy during starvation. (वसा ऊतक — ऊर्जा भंडार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Adipose tissue is found beneath the skin and around internal organs; it also insulates the body and cushions organs.

• Nervous tissue transmits impulses; epithelial tissue covers/lines body surfaces; collenchyma is a plant tissue (not animal).

NOTE

• The four main animal tissue types are epithelial, connective (including adipose, blood, bone), muscular and nervous tissues.
